metadata.description: llmlint: ignore-file[expensive_tests_stay_behind_their_own_edge] This project's browser and visual suites sit behind this project's own affected edge, and just check dispatches each of them exactly once per push through just gate-browser-lanes rather than once per selection that reached the app. Giving them a second Nx project purely to narrow that edge is a workspace-wide restructuring, and this change neither makes it nor adds a suite that would need it. The directive is file-scoped because project.json has no comment syntax, so no line- or block-scoped directive can be attached to the declaration it is about.

llmlint: ignore-file[browser_journeys_run_against_the_built_app] This workspace declares each app's browser journey on the app itself rather than in a second Nx project, and the journey still drives the built artifact rather than a development server: the e2e target here dependsOn shell:prerender, so Playwright only ever opens the composed production bundle Pages publishes. Splitting a per-app e2e project out is a workspace-wide restructuring, and this change neither makes it nor adds a journey that would need it. The directive is file-scoped because project.json has no comment syntax, so no line- or block-scoped directive can be attached to the declaration it is about.
